m1.quote: Ambitious scope is often where solo/small-team open source projects either stall or become impossible to audit properly — which matters a lot given this thing also runs an OAuth server and handles credentials.
m1.note: Asserts small-team scope makes the security-critical code impossible to audit/scrutinize properly.

m2.note: Notes the built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization server as scope creep and audit surface, but never claims they should have delegated to an external IdP or invokes 'don't roll your own auth'.

m3.note: Engages directly with the DOI-registered benchmark and criticizes it as self-designed and vendor-authored, which is not a claim that evidence is absent.

m4.quote: That's a coherent ecosystem, but it also means the value proposition is maximized only if you adopt this specific vendor's opinionated stack; the PostgreSQL-only fallback is explicitly framed as the lesser option ("gateways, knowledge layer, memory, portal... without DataHub or Trino").
m4.note: Despite acknowledging the PostgreSQL-only shape, it frames DataHub/Trino adoption as a vendor lock-in and ecosystem coupling cost under an explicit 'Vendor lock-in' heading.
